name: Elias Earle
bio: A Representative from South Carolina; born in Frederick County, Va., June 19, 1762; attended private school; moved to Greenville County, S.C., in September 1787; was one of the earliest ironmasters of the South, and prospected and negotiated in the iron region of Georgia; member of South Carolina state house of representatives, 1794-1797; member of the South Carolina state senate in 1800; elected as a Democratic Republican to the Ninth Congress (March 4, 1805-March 3, 1807); unsuccessful candidate for reelection to the Tenth Congress in 1806; elected as a Democratic Republican to the Twelfth and and to the succeeding Congress (March 4, 1811-March 3, 1815); unsuccessful candidate for reelection to the Fourteenth Congress in 1814; postmaster, Centerville, S.C., 1815-1817; elected as a Democratic Republican to the Fifteenth and to the succeeding Congress (March 4, 1817-March 3, 1821); unsuccessful candidate for reelection to the Seventeenth Congress in 1820; died on May 19, 1823, in Centerville, S.C.; interment in Old Earle Cemetery, Buncombe Road, Greenville, S.C.
